claims.statement: Databrowser's warning documents end-of-life December 31st 2023 and references the 2022-03-21 changelog, which identifies Integrated Search as its successor.
GDPR Platform's warning and the 2025-04-02 changelog document scheduled end-of-life June 30th 2025, but the 2025-04-11 changelog records early retirement.
The deprecations document lists Databrowser and GDPR Platform and explicitly instructs readers not to use deprecated features.
The Databrowser guide embeds swagger_databrowser.yaml, whose declared endpoints are internal-only and may change or be removed at any time, rather than a stable public API commitment.

GDPR Platform is documented as Management Studio for configuration and datahub access, a datahub for collection/connection/storage, and a public subject-facing DAP for requests, data, and consents; management access is through the Sesam portal subscription.

Databrowser's narrative file configuration processes uploaded numeric layers in ascending override order and the end-user /sesam/data/databrowser.ini last, overriding /sesam/conf/databrowser.ini and numbered layers; the extra layered upload API is not exposed in the end-user GUI.

The Databrowser guide distinguishes shared defaults, installation-specific files, and Redis-backed GUI changes, and supports bulk Redis configuration editing/copying; these descriptions do not specify Redis precedence against every numeric file layer.

The narrative Databrowser configuration-file API requires JWT authentication enabled, an Authorization-header JWT granting Admin, and describes its example token as generated for the configured subscription.

The Databrowser configuration narrative declares /configuration/<confignumber>/databrowser.ini but its example uses /configuration/conf/1/databrowser.ini, consistent with Swagger's /configuration/conf/{config_layer}/{config_file_path}; the documentation therefore disagrees on the layered route form.
Databrowser's internal configuration-file GET specification returns an empty response body when the requested file does not exist.

Internal Databrowser configuration PUT/DELETE can return HTTP 200 with configuration errors; the response contains is-valid-config, current-user-would-be-locked-out, and config-errors, and errors concern the full configuration set rather than only the changed file.
The internal configuration-file API specifies HTTP 403 refusal when PUT or DELETE would prevent the current user from making further configuration changes.
The internal configuration-file validate_only parameter defaults false and, when true, performs validation without changing configuration.

Swagger documents config_file_path as an inaccurately modeled remainder-of-path and explicitly says it should not be URL-escaped, illustrating nested file segments under a numbered configuration layer.

Databrowser's /admin_index exposes administrative configuration, data-type, and logging pages; GUI logging changes reset on server restart and permanent changes require installation-specific production.ini.

Databrowser's use_x_remote_user_header selects external OIDC when false and trusted X-Remote-User authentication when true; the latter is documented as safe only behind an authenticating proxy that sets the header.

Header authentication maps a username to a session email through Solr fields configured by x_remote_user_username_psi and x_remote_user_email_psi, falling back to an email-like username when no email is found.
Databrowser authorization searches configured email fields for the session email and stores matching item IDs plus IDs referenced through psi* fields in session psis.

In Databrowser OPEN mode items without configured AUTH_FIELDS are available to all; AUTHENTICATED restricts this to authenticated users, excludes anonymous users, and both modes exclude items containing configured authorization fields.
Databrowser AUTHORIZED mode requires AUTH_FIELDS and restricts authenticated searches to items with the specified authorization fields and authorization or ID fields matching the session psis values.
Sesam-portal JWT authentication is enabled by jwt_authentication_subscription_ids, listing accepted subscriptions or using * to accept JWTs from all subscriptions.
Ordinary Databrowser JWT users remain subject to Solr authorization, while JWT group:Admin grants access to all Solr documents and configuration editing.

The JWT narrative describes /jwt_login GET as a token form and POST as storing parsed credentials in a server-side session then redirecting; Swagger labels GET development/testing-only and POST as Management Studio access.
Databrowser authentication and GDPR Platform configuration share the same OIDC provider include, which itself carries the Databrowser end-of-life warning rather than GDPR Platform's distinct warning.
Shared OIDC configuration requires unique provider_id values, consumer_key and consumer_secret, and discovery URL or inline metadata; the docs prefer discovery metadata URLs.

Shared OIDC options default user_id_attribute to sub, contactinfo_attribute to email, and scope to openid profile email; userinfo can be disabled in favor of IDToken extraction, and the docs recommend Google email and Microsoft upn identity claims.
The shared OIDC allow_unverified_email option defaults true and can be disabled for email-based providers that do not already verify addresses.
The documented OIDC browser flow returns an authorization code to the DAP backend /login_callback/<provider_id>, using the configured provider ID, and post-logout redirects use the backend base URL.

The GDPR Excel setup uses Purpose and Data type sheets; purpose metadata includes activity, legal-ground, source/sharing, retention-day, criteria, and language fields, and purposes appear as subject navigation tabs with opt-in/out for consent-type purposes.

GDPR data types describe type/system, description, Personal or Related level, notification contacts, and a generated x-mark matrix allowing multiple purposes per type; contact email lists must not have whitespace around commas.

Purpose and data-type spreadsheet IDs are computed and must not be manually edited; the data-type ID description allows a maximum of 32 characters while Type/System descriptions require their combination to be less than 32 including whitespace.

Uploading the GDPR setup updates platform structures and DAP types/purposes after potentially a few minutes, inspectable in gdpr-data-type and gdpr-purpose; shared-URL setup retrieval has configurable cron scheduling defaulting to midnight UTC.
Default GDPR subject login sends an OTP to an email address or phone number, and the portal guide says it expires at session end or after an unspecified idle interval; OIDC is an alternative.

GDPR access_request_contactinfo can require a notification destination at request time when authentication supplies none; supported configuration types are email and mobile_phone with user choice for multiple types and validation by the OTP email/phone regex options.
GDPR extra_access_request_fields is empty by default and adds required unique subject-identifier fields whose headers and tooltips are resolved through localization.

Historical GDPR documentation gives both selected-domain-name.sesamdata.com and gdpr-dap-subscription_id backend URL forms, with the portal guide directing operators to Network for the backend URL; these examples do not establish one universal hostname convention.

A manual GDPR access request notifies all unique spreadsheet contacts, and handlers must be registered Sesam portal users, GDPR Platform members, and granted GDPR operations to access the request template workflow.

The manual GDPR request template's DataSubject identifiers and UTC request timestamp must remain unchanged; data-type/system sheets require a unique id column and one row per source-data row, followed by upload through the Access request template form.

The documented manual request upload encrypts subject data with the subject public key, stores it in the GDPR datahub, and sends it to DAP for decryption with a private key stored only on the subject computer; the automation guide separately describes importing copies of source data into the datahub.
Manual GDPR uploads notify subjects with registered email addresses after a half-hour delay for DAP propagation, and each separately uploaded completed spreadsheet triggers its own notification.

Configured subject data edits and consent grant/revocation generate GDPR change notifications to originating data-type contacts; downloadable lists include subject/data IDs, old/new values, and timestamp, and manual accepted changes require source updates and refilled/reuploaded spreadsheets by GDPR operations handlers.

The GDPR portal narrative treats whole-subject deletion as revocation of all consents and a special change request; manual handlers must delete linked source data then upload an updated spreadsheet, and the narrative says data pertaining to revoked consent should be deleted.
Historical GDPR guides permit automated change/deletion integrations that trigger mutations directly in source systems, rather than documenting requests alone as completion of those mutations.

Internal Swagger POST /accessrequests requires publicKey, boolean deleteRequest, and lang, accepts configured extraFields and contactinfo, and returns an empty JSON object on success rather than subject records.

Internal DAP /accessrequest_login is called after login for a prior request and associates readable request data with its original publicKey; /accessrequests_update takes that key with update, delete, or add-purpose-to-access-request actions.

The internal DAP specification provides document-specific GET /changerequests plus search/item-detail, GDPR download, and client field-formatting routes; field configuration supports client-side formatting of decrypted fields.

The GDPR developer integration APIs are defined datasets with JSON Push receiver/publisher endpoints, including gdpr-subject-in/out and gdpr-access-request-in/out; these are distinct from Databrowser's internal UI routes.

JSON Push uses HTTP POST, batching, and JSON arrays even for single entities, supports incremental/full synchronization, and defines full-sync sequence conflicts with 409 and restart behavior, unlike DAP access-request creation's single object schema.

GDPR automation adds TypeID, Identifiers, and Exclude while leaving the purpose sheet unchanged; Personal identifiers match subjects directly, Related identifiers form parent chains ending in Personal records, Exclude filters properties, and registered custom-subject-data source datasets feed request matching.
The GDPR developer guide says TypeID matches dataset ID, while the getting-started guide says TypeID matches rdf:type, leaving a material configuration-description discrepancy.

The GDPR subject contract requires a unique subject-id and nonempty identifier list for matching instances of a subject; custom-subject merges with receiver input into gdpr-subject and is externally exposed through its publisher.

GDPR developer contracts merge custom-consent, custom-subject-consent, custom-purpose, custom-purpose-type, custom-data-type, and custom-policy datasets with corresponding receiver inputs into platform datasets exposed through publishers; purpose-type explicitly chooses the newest version for matching purpose-type-id.

gdpr-subject-consent records subject-specific affirmative/negative consent choices and selection time; its prototype names gdpr-subject-consent:valid-from while its property table names gdpr-consent:valid-from.
The purpose-type input API paragraph names gdpr-purpose-in while the accompanying URL names gdpr-purpose-type-in.
The GDPR data-type prototype uses language-prefixed description keys such as gdpr-data-type:en-description, but the property table uses suffix keys such as gdpr-data-type:description-en.

Dataset GDPR access requests require access-request-id, user-id, and PGP public-key for encrypting collected request data before storage/processing; contactinfo-type chooses email or phone_number, delete-request is a string false/true default false, extra properties pass to output, and platform-assigned outgoing UTC timestamp overwrites input.

The experimental gdpr-access-request-subject-data-in receiver may not be available in all installations, requires an existing request ID/data-type ID, reporter and entities with unique IDs/data objects, encrypts with the request's subject public key, and has no output API because decryption is on the originating device.

Unstructured GDPR document-source microservices provide metadata and binary-download APIs normalized by importing pipes; custom-documents merges sources for extraction, and the index stores extracted text/properties except metadata without storing original files in that indexing process.

Unstructured GDPR searches run at new access-request creation using subject properties, are point-in-time, and are not automatically rerun for newly indexed documents; the search paragraph spells custom-document singular despite the internal dataset being named custom-documents.

Every unstructured GDPR search match requires manual vetting before DAP disclosure due to false positives or other subjects' data; reviewers can remove rows, withhold files by removing extract-content links, and replace text/metadata before uploading the reviewed spreadsheet.

After unstructured GDPR vetting, document metadata is encrypted with the subject public key and transmitted to DAP; a remaining extract-content link also causes the file to be fetched, encrypted, and transmitted for client-side decryption/download.

The unstructured document extract-content URL is documented as not challenging for authentication and restricted to a local network reachable only by GDPR Platform, with the microservice proxying backend credentials; original-url must challenge for needed authentication and be reachable by human reviewers.

GDPR custom-translations changes require preserving template and environment macros and starting the saved pipe; affected notification/object translations apply to new emissions rather than already emitted objects.

The inspected repository pull-request workflow builds documentation using make html, and README documents the same preview command; this does not establish runtime legacy-service integration test results.
